subject: Dedicated capacity: clarifying GPU choice, TPS targets & token mix
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: clarifying GPU choice, TPS targets & token mix

Jordan / Ava — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a Dedicated pool and confirm deployment mode (Dedicated in VPC vs Private on-prem). Attached is the capacity workbook I mentioned.

Call recap (what we heard)
- Target deployment: Dedicated capacity inside a customer VPC (you still evaluating Private on-prem, but procurement prefers Dedicated first).
- Steady-state TPS: ~20 requests/sec (you flagged steady production is relatively even overnight).
- Peak TPS: short bursts up to ~80 req/sec (15-minute bursts during triage windows).
- Token mix: estimated average ~750 tokens/request; some jobs are long (2.5k–3k) but majority are short (200–400).
- Latency SLO: 95/99 targets unclear; you called out desire to keep 95th < 200–300ms for interactive flows.
- Security: PHI and encryption at rest required; model weights cannot leave customer-controlled VPC without explicit controls.

Questions / asks for sizing
1) Confirm the steady/peak numbers above (steady vs sustained 1‑hr average).
2) Specify the % split short vs long requests (gives us concurrency profile).
3) Any hard constraints on latency at p99 vs p95?
4) Preference on GPU family: do you have a pre-existing procurement bias toward A100 vs H100? We can size for either and show tradeoffs (replication vs quantization).

Preliminary thoughts (for discussion)
- With an 8k-context model and the token mix above, H100 80GB gives the cleanest path for headroom and long-context throughput; A100 80GB + 4-bit quantization (nf4/awq) can be much more cost efficient but adds validation risk for correctness/regulatory sign-off.
- For your peak bursts we typically recommend configuring autoscaled dedicated pools with reserved baseline capacity to cover steady TPS and scheduled burst capacity (or burst via committed + temporary surge).

Next steps
- Please review and correct the numbers in the attached workbook.
- If you can share a 24‑hour request histogram (counts by token size), Karthik can run a quick model-level throughput calc and give GPU-count guidance.
- I'll propose two times for a deep-sizing session with Karthik and your infra lead.

Attachments: lumencare_capacity_workbook_v2.xlsx (workbook), redwood_intro_deck.pdf (product brief)

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks Rishi — great summary. A few corrections / clarifications from our side: 
- Steady-state TPS is closer to 15 req/sec (we over-indexed on the product call).
- Peak TPS: bursts up to 60 req/sec (usually 10–20 minute bursts during morning syncs).
- Token mix: ~70% short interactions (~150–300 tokens), ~30% long (2.5k–3k tokens). Average ~650 tokens/request across the mix.
- Model context: we plan to use an 8k context model for summarization + retrieval augmented flows.
- Security: PHI requirements mean we need encryption at rest + customer KMS; we also need a deployment where model artifacts do not leave our VPC without a signed exception.

Procurement note (cc'd): we will need an initial quote for Dedicated capacity in our preferred cloud region (us-west-2) and an outline of the private/VPC deployment options and the minimum commitment term.

Jordan Hayes
Head of Platform Engineering, Lumencare Health

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity: clarifying GPU choice, TPS targets & token mix

Jordan / Rishi — digging into the numbers you just provided. High-level recommendations and a quick back-of-envelope for Dedicated sizing: 

Assumptions based on Jordan's update:
- steady 15 TPS, peak 60 TPS (10–20 minute bursts)
- token distribution: 70% short (200 avg), 30% long (2.6k avg)
- target p95 latency: ~200ms; p99 ideally <500ms for interactive flows but we should set expectations on very long requests
- model: 8k context, decoder-only architecture (we'll confirm exact model family)

GPU guidance (tradeoffs):
- H100 80GB: best single-GPU headroom for 8k context and long requests; simpler to meet p95/p99 without aggressive quantization.
- A100 80GB: viable if we adopt nf4/awq 4-bit quantization and validate quality; more replicas needed to hit same latency/consistency under long-token workloads.

Concurrency and replication strategy:
- For your mixture, we should target ~45–55 concurrent inference streams at peak to keep queueing low (rough calc: peak token-rate / per-GPU token throughput).
- Two-tier pool: baseline reserved (cover steady 15 TPS) + burst pool (auto-scale to cover 60 TPS peaks). Recommend baseline = capacity for ~20 TPS (safety), burst headroom to 70 TPS.

Estimated starting footprint (pilot -> production):
- Pilot (smoke + validation): 2 x H100 (or 3 x A100 with quant) as a small dedicated pool for end-to-end validation and correctness tests (includes KMS/VPC config).
- Production (conservative estimate): 6 x H100 80GB (replicas/sharding) OR 9 x A100 80GB (with validated 4-bit quant) to meet p95/p99 and burst concurrency. These are conservative and we can refine with actual histograms.

Action items for accurate sizing:
1) Rishi/Jordan: Share a 24‑hour histogram by token bucket (bins: <256, 256–1024, 1024–4k, >4k).
2) Jordan: Confirm hard p99 SLA requirement (if any) and whether slower offline jobs can be offloaded to a cheaper pool.
3) Procurement: preferred term length (monthly vs annual) and any approved GPU families.

Attachment: I updated a copy of the capacity workbook with a tab for H100 vs A100 delta (see Drive link) and rough GPU count so Lumencare can review.

Thanks — happy to run a short calculation in tomorrow's deep-dive if we get the histogram.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
